touches.text: The verdict's instrument run is a seal-grade run, so it runs where the sealer runs (9.4.2.3.3.1), under bubblewrap. A box without bubblewrap (Windows) asks for it and does not run it itself. A bwrap-only tooth reads not-run on such a box, never red; its outcome is the sealer's. - CC

Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead.

A seal is host independent: one record per proof, whichever box asks. Seals are made by one sealing machine in the cairn device, and there is only ever one cairn (until a laptop dies and a backup takes over), so there is one sealer. A box that is not cairn's home asks the sealer instead of writing its own seal.
Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged.
INTENTION:
WHOS: who settles what. Why? Because we found we needed a boundary on who is the first person to try and reconcile conflicting points for a given thing.
CONFIDENCE: what each mark means. Wy? Because Claude tends to assume 0 or 100%.
INTENTION:
INTENTION:

The ticket IS its own manager. It carries its workflow and status, and asks each gate whether it can transit. If refused, it gets itself back to design for fixing. If no handler is available to ask, it throws a trouble and waits until we decide. Design is CC and Akien until the outline is implemented; a design agent comes after that. Until then a refused ticket waits in the trouble lane, which both read when a session opens, and nothing posts to a design verb that no machine answers.
Commit often. WHY: so we never wind up with stray files or incomplete work.

Prebuild face: the chart chain, eight machines, each answering one question before a build begins: orient (what is asked, where does it live), constrain (what bounds it), survey (what already exists), decompose (how does it split), triage (what first, by what standard), hypothesize (what do we expect, how would we know we're wrong), validate (what does DONE mean, measured), and after the build, verdict (what done actually meant).
tester
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
Hollow runs: proves a proof goes red when the build is removed.
The chart chain machines (9.3.2): orient, constrain, survey, decompose, triage, hypothesize, validate, verdict.

Three instrument runs at once share the repo, /tmp, the network and git, so a red can come from a neighbour. HYPOTHESIS: a red is re-run once, alone, before it is recorded; both readings stand on the verdict, and a red that turns green alone is a contention red. Its WATCHME brings cc_0 every re-run's pair of readings, so the hypothesis is reviewed against them (0.6.1). - CC

An instrument is the literal command the sealer runs, never prose about how to run one. Why? The verdict must come from a hand the builder did not guide (9.4.2.2), and prose needs a reader to guess the command; validate moves to deterministic code (9.3.2.1). CC's decision, Q#126, on "we are moving away from prose ... we need things we can check" -amm. - CC
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.

CORE VALUES: written for Igor, and they hold in the process that builds him too (Law 2). Code carries them as CoreValuesMixin (cairn/tools/base/core_values.py), pinned to these words. Held at about 90%: they guide, and a measured reason can outweigh one in a given case.

conflicts.ticket_says: Find why cairn/devices/codemother/machines/verdict/proofs/test_an_instrument_runs_under_the_seal.py reds on Windows and fix it so the proof reseals green.
conflicts.why: 9.4.8.1 states: 'A box without bubblewrap (bwrap) (Windows) asks for it and does not run it itself. A bwrap-only tooth reads not-run on such a box, never red; its outcome is the sealer's.' The ticket shows the proof teeth ARE red on Windows, violating the outline's constraint that bwrap-only teeth should never be red on Windows. If the fix allows Windows to run the instrument directly (instead of delegating to the central sealer), it contradicts the outline's requirement that Windows 'does not run it itself.' The fix must either skip these teeth on Windows (read not-run), or ensure the central sealer runs them and Windows receives the green seal—not make Windows capable of running them independently.
